title: Berlin Weekly Markets - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin markets run on fixed weekdays, not every day.** There are around a hundred of them across the city, and each one trades on the same one, two or three days every week. Turning up on the wrong day means an empty square.

**Most of them are a morning habit.** The two big produce squares, Winterfeldtplatz and Karl-August-Platz, both open at 08:00 and start packing up in the early afternoon. Karl-August-Platz is finished at 13:00 on a Wednesday.
**Saturday is peak, with nine markets worth the trip.** They stagger their opening between 08:00 and 10:30 and every one of them is shut by 18:00.
**Nothing at all trades on a Sunday.** No weekly food market in Berlin opens on a Sunday and Markthalle Neun is closed too. Sunday is the flea market day instead.
**Monday is nearly empty.** Only the covered hall, Markthalle Neun, runs a market on a Monday, from 12:00 to 18:00.

**Three markets break the morning rule.** Maybachufer opens 11:00 to 18:30 on Tuesdays and Fridays, Arkonaplatz runs 12:00 to 19:00 on a Friday, and the Kollwitzplatz organic market runs 12:00 to 19:00 on a Thursday.
**Thursday runs latest.** Street Food Thursday inside Markthalle Neun trades 17:00 to 22:00, the only market hours in the city that reach into the evening.
**Bring cash and a bag.** Berlin markets are the most reliably cash-only corner of the city, there is rarely a machine on the square, and plastic bags are not handed out free in Germany.
